# Geophysical Fluid Dynamics

The sequence derives the stochastically stirred barotropic vorticity equation
from continuum mass and momentum conservation. It introduces rotating frames,
absolute circulation, layer potential vorticity, constant-depth reduction,
spherical inversion, energy and enstrophy, damping, and finite-memory forcing.
The assumptions of each reduction are stated separately.

The mathematical prerequisites are [vector calculus](../01-vector-calculus/index.qmd),
[orthogonal expansions](../02-harmonic-analysis/index.qmd), and
[spectral numerical methods](../03-pdes/spectral-methods.qmd). The fluid chapters
also define the operators and probability needed for their derivations.

These chapters share a source with the
[physical-prerequisites document](https://github.com/tglanz/climatology/blob/main/presentations/physical-prerequisites/physical-prerequisites.md).
The book includes the parcel-kinematics and transport derivations, while
cross-referencing its vector-calculus chapters for the shared operator theory.
It retains the general fluid theory and excludes the companion's implementation appendix. Equation labels prefixed P
refer to the companion document's stable chapter-equation numbers, independently
of the book's chapter ordering.

Primary sources are @Vallis2006, @BarotropicNotes, and @ArfkenWeber2005.
The specific finite-memory stirring process comes from @VallisEtAl2004.
The angular convention here is longitude $\lambda$, latitude $\phi$;
the mathematical chapters use colatitude $\theta=\pi/2-\varphi$, latitude $\varphi$, and longitude $\lambda$.
This is a change of coordinates, not a change in the harmonic normalization:
$\int |Y_\ell^m|^2d\omega=1$ in both.
